module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 513

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/513](https://www.erdosproblems.com/513)
 - [ClHa64] Clunie, J. and Hayman, W. K., The maximum term of a power series. J. Analyse Math.
  (1964), 143-186.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Nat Real
open Filter Polynomial

namespace Erdos513

noncomputable def ratio (r : ℝ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  (⨆ n, ‖iteratedDeriv n f 0 * (n ! : ℝ)⁻¹ * r ^ n‖) / (⨆ z : {z : ℂ // ‖z‖ = r}, ‖f z‖)

/-- Let `f` be a transcendental entire function. What is the greatest possible value of
`liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_513 : answer(sorry) =
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) := by
  sorry

/-- For all transcendental entire function `f`, `liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop ≤ 2 / π - c`
for some `c > 0`. This is proved in [ClHa64]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_513.variants.upper_bound : ∃ c > 0,
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) ≤ 2 / π - c := by
  sorry

/-- For all transcendental entire function `f`, `liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop > 1 / 2`. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_513.variants.lower_bound :
    ⨆ f : {f : ℂ → ℂ // Transcendental ℂ[X] f ∧ Differentiable ℂ f},
    (liminf (fun r : ℝ => ratio r f) atTop) > 1 / 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos513

findings.description: The docstring at line 55 says every transcendental entire function has liminf(ratio r f) > 1/2. The Lean statement correctly says that the supremum of these liminfs exceeds 1/2, equivalently that some such function has liminf > 1/2. The universal claim in the docstring is false: f(z) = exp(z) has liminf 0. The supremum/existence equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/bounds.lean without using the file's sorry theorems.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/513 defines B as 'the supremum of all such values' and says Kövári observed that B > 1/2. It also records the stronger Clunie–Hayman bound 4/7 < B. These are bounds on B, not lower bounds for every function.
findings.suggested_fix: Change only the docstring to say that the supremum over transcendental entire functions is greater than 1/2, or equivalently that there exists a transcendental entire function with liminf(ratio r f) > 1/2. Keep the Lean statement unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The subtype shared by the main theorem and both variants expresses 'transcendental entire' using Transcendental ℂ[X] f together with Differentiable ℂ f, rather than explicitly excluding polynomial functions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Polynomial.instAlgebraPi sends a polynomial p to the function z ↦ p(z). Thus algebraicity here means that a nonzero bivariate polynomial P satisfies P(z,f(z)) = 0 identically; this interpretation was checked in Lean. An entire algebraic function is a polynomial: outside a sufficiently large disk, the leading coefficient of P in its second variable is nonzero, and the polynomial root bound gives polynomial growth for f. Cauchy estimates then force all sufficiently high Taylor coefficients to vanish. Conversely, a polynomial function q satisfies the nonzero relation Y − q(X) = 0. Therefore the subtype describes exactly the source's transcendental entire functions.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/513 (full formulas, remarks, and current status, retrieved through Jina Reader)

Yixin He and Quanyu Tang, Generalizing the Clunie–Hayman construction in an Erdős maximum-term problem, arXiv:2602.12217v1, §1 and the transcendental-entire construction in §2; https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12217 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/2602.12217
W. K. Hayman and E. F. Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory, Problem 2.14 and its update; LaTeX source https://arxiv.org/e-print/1809.07200
review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Apart from the lower-bound docstring, the mathematical statements match the sources. Successful Lean experiments in boundary.lean, semantics.lean, and bounds.lean under /workspace/review/ verify the Taylor expansion encoded by the numerator, exclusion of polynomial functions, radius-zero and negative-radius behavior, compact-circle boundedness, 0 ≤ ratio ≤ 1 for entire functions at positive radii, bounded liminfs, and boundedness of the outer supremum. Nonpositive radii do not affect the limit atTop. The source still marks the exact value as open; subsequent lower-bound improvements do not invalidate either solved variant. The original Clunie–Hayman full text was paywalled, but its relevant bounds are explicitly corroborated by the problem page, Hayman–Lingham Problem 2.14(c), and He–Tang §1. The reviewed file's hash agrees with the requested commit.
